items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: Joe came into this band, I think the day after Christmas in 1954.

ctx.x: And Joe will be watching that, that’s good. Anything else you want to add for us?

Well I only remember one thing in particular about Joe. Joe came into this band, I think the day after Christmas in 1954. He and Sonny Payne came in on the same day. And they started being roommates. And you have never seen an odder couple than those two, you know, I mean the stories that came from that union were enough to fill a book, and I mean I could like say all night long about the things that they did that were awesomely funny. But Joe transformed this band from like a great band that was working but not…
And the words Count Basie-Joe Williams were magic. There was a guaranteed full house, lines around the corner. Count Basie-Joe Williams.
